conversations.title: Thousands in Amsterdam for boisterous WorldPride in shadow of Berlin attack
conversations.reply: Amsterdam getting it right for WorldPride is a great start, but it's frustrating that so many other events still don't get accessibility right, it's like they're missing the point of the celebration.

conversations.title: Letters: Businesses should improve access for people with disabilities
conversations.reply: It's ridiculous that we're still having to ask for basic accessibility in 2026, businesses should be leading the way, not dragging their feet.

conversations.title: Syria’s first disability football tournament takes the field, in photos
conversations.reply: This tournament looks amazing, so great to see people having the chance to take part and have fun.

conversations.title: July is Disability Pride month
conversations.reply: I'm so glad you're flying the flag for Disability Pride month, it's great to see people being proud of who they are.

conversations.title: Avoid this one dating habit that has 'zero ability to predict if a relationship will be happy or stable,' says relationship coach
conversations.reply: It's so true that focusing on the wrong things in dating can lead to disappointment, we need to look beyond the surface level and find what really matters.

conversations.title: L.A. Affairs: I had strict dating rules: No teachers, no only children and no one from the Valley
conversations.reply: I love that you had your own dating rules, but it's sad that for many of us, the rules are made by others, it's time we took control of our own dating lives.

conversations.title: Wounded in combat, they met in rehab and fell in love
conversations.reply: This story is a beautiful reminder that love can find us in unexpected places, and that people with disabilities deserve the same chance at love as everyone else.

conversations.title: VA Says It Processed 2 Million Disability Claims Faster Than Ever
conversations.reply: Faster claims processing is a step in the right direction, but it's only the beginning, we need to make sure people are getting the support they need, not just the paperwork.

Task: today's Able2Love engagement round (2026-08-02). You are working in my logged-in browser as the app's accounts: @Able2LoveApp on X, @able2loveapp on Instagram.

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.

- Amsterdam getting it right for WorldPride is a great start, but it's frustrating that so many other events still don't get accessibility right, it's like they're missing the point of the celebration.

- Faster claims processing is a step in the right direction, but it's only the beginning, we need to make sure people are getting the support they need, not just the paperwork.
